idea: N wedges arranged radially (a rosette), each wedge built as a stack of T annular 'step' tiers -- every tier is a filled annular sector, narrower than the tier below it, so the wedge's silhouette staircases inward as it rises outward from the centre, like a ziggurat's setback profile viewed in plan around a circle. Wedge/tier count fixed once per video from DENSITY; only a rigid rotation of the whole rosette changes over time, so total covered area never varies. A genuinely different construction principle from every other engine in the pool: not an arithmetic sieve (primespiral), not a substitution/subdivision system (quasicrystal), not a discrete cellular-automaton local rule (automaton), not an implicit wave-interference zero-set (chladni) -- a single irrational-angle increment rule applied sequentially, densely packing each cluster disk. reason: Three earlier design iterations of this exact engine FAILED the mandatory novelty gate before a fourth passed -- recorded in full because the underlying lesson (the colour-blind fingerprint descriptor can measure very different-LOOKING compositions as structurally close, and a generically 'moderately-covered aperiodic blob' composition can land near an unrelated engine that itself sits centrally in feature space) is a new failure mode not previously documented. A genuinely different construction principle from every other engine in the pool: not an arithmetic sieve (primespiral), not a substitution/subdivision system that repartitions a fixed area (quasicrystal), not a discrete cellular-automaton local rule (automaton), not an implicit wave-interference zero-set (chladni), not a golden-angle packing rule (phyllotaxis) -- a recursive branching growth process. inspirationSource: The geodesic dome -- Buckminster Fuller's architectural structure built by triangulating an icosahedron's faces ('frequency' subdivision) and projecting every new vertex outward onto a circumscribing sphere, distributing structural load evenly across a lattice of near-equal triangles. Category was 'random architectural or typographic movement' by the firing-minute-mod-category-count method; an open WebSearch for a geometric architectural structural principle surfaced geodesic domes and their icosahedral/triangulation basis directly. The pool was also explicitly 3D-poor at the time (4 of 25 engines real WebGL), and this inspiration genuinely supports a real lit-3D rendering (not forced), so it was built as one. https://science.howstuffworks.com/engineering/structural/geodesic-dome.htm ; https://www.cjfearnley.com/fuller-faq-4.html
idea: Icosahedron subdivided N times (each new edge midpoint re-projected onto the unit sphere -- the real Fuller-dome 'frequency' construction), cut below a fixed latitude for a recognisable dome (not full-sphere) silhouette, rendered as ONE continuous faceted mesh in a single WebGL draw call (per-vertex colour, not per-object) so hundreds of differently-coloured triangles render fast enough for the render budget. A genuinely different 3D composition from every other real-WebGL engine in the pool: not sparse orbiting solids (solids3d), not a grid of independently-spinning cubes (lattice3d), not lit tori/rings (torusrings3d) -- one large continuous faceted surface, lit and depth-sorted as a single solid mesh.
reason: Icosahedron vertex/face data and the subdivision's edge-sharing/winding consistency were verified offline (every edge shared by exactly 2 triangles, no gaps) before writing any rendering code, the same discipline CLAUDE.md documents for quasicrystal.html's Robinson-triangle formulas. Three real bugs found only by rendering and running validate.js, the third needing extensive iteration: (1) a centroid-only dome-cut filter let through boundary triangles with one vertex well below the cut, rendering as thin dark slivers at the rim -- fixed by requiring ALL three vertices to clear the cut plane. (2) Colouring each face by LONGITUDE (theta) failed validate.js's brightness-trend check (projected +208 luma): as the dome spins about its own vertical axis, depth occlusion exposes a different half of the theta-based colour wheel each cycle, and since HSL hue affects luma at fixed S/L, which half is visible swings average brightness -- the same 'hue affects luma' lesson quasicrystal.html already documents, reached via 3D depth-occlusion visibility (the failure class CLAUDE.md documents for solids3d.html) rather than a re-randomised parameter. Fixed by tying hue to LATITUDE (phi) instead, which is invariant under a Y-axis rotation. (3) That fix then made the dome look visually self-similar under rotation to the fast-motion check (every longitude at a given latitude is now the same colour), the same underlying problem torusrings3d.html hit from its own silhouette-invariant spin -- validateEngine() failed fastMotion on 5/5 tested seeds even after raising the rotation rate. Root-caused (confirmed via a diagnostic dump) to the fast-motion floor being dominated by the black-background/lit-dome contrast, which a silhouette-invariant spin can never move enough of. Fixed with THREE independent, coverage-neutral motion/colour levers layered together after several rounds of parameter tuning: a small longitude-based SATURATION ripple (not hue -- saturation has far less effect on luma at fixed lightness), a bounded dual-frequency light-direction oscillation (never fully back-lighting the dome, unlike an early full 360-degree sweep that reintroduced the brightness-trend bug), and a small continuous (never reset per-cycle, to avoid an uncorrelated-phase-jump variant of the same bug) tilt wobble. Verified: validateEngine() across a 16-seed stress battery (1-13, 17, 42, 99, plus the CLI's actual default seed 12345) -- 13/16 passed, including the production-default seed. The 3 residual failures (seed 3: +54.9 brightness; seeds 42/99: fast-motion) persisted across many different structural adjustments (hemisphere vs 5/8-sphere cut, multiple tilt/light amplitude combinations) without a clean elimination, consistent with CLAUDE.md's own documented, accepted residual-failure-rate for real 3D depth-occlusion engines (solids3d.html, torusrings3d.html) rather than an uncaught bug -- curated engines are a design-time check only and never run validate.js at production runtime. avgSat 46.7-62.3 throughout (well above the 22 minimum), zero near-white pixels, projectedHourRenderMin 37.9min on the default seed (well inside the CI budget). inspirationSource: The Voderberg tiling -- Heinz Voderberg's 1936 discovery, the first spiral tiling ever devised: a single congruent non-convex nonagon, repeated and rotated by a fixed increment as it marches outward, forms two interlocking spiral arms (point-symmetric through the centre) that tile the plane with no gaps, using just one repeated shape. inspirationSource: Twill weave (and its 'broken twill' variant, herringbone) -- the textile construction rule behind denim and herringbone tweed: a grid of warp/weft threads where the weft goes over a fixed number of warp threads, then under a fixed number, and this over/under pattern shifts by exactly one warp position every row, producing the signature diagonal 'wale' ribs as an emergent side-effect rather than a drawn diagonal. idea: A single square grid where each cell's binary over/under state is determined by a simple modular shift rule: isOver(r,c) = ((dir*c + r) mod period) < over, where period = over+under threads and dir flips sign every bandWidthCells columns to produce herringbone's chevron/fishbone bands. The over/under shift rule was verified OFFLINE before writing any rendering code (a standalone script printed the resulting grid as ASCII and confirmed algebraically that row r+1's pattern at column c exactly equals row r's pattern at column c+1 -- the defining diagonal-shift invariant -- for both the plain-twill and herringbone-banded rules), the same discipline this pool's quasicrystal.html/geodome.html/hilbertweave.html already established. A genuinely different construction principle from every other engine in the pool: not a substitution/subdivision system (quasicrystal/voderberg), not several independently-angled overlaid band families (widmanstatten), not a proximity partition (voronoimosaic), not a single recursively-defined path (hilbertweave) -- a single grid with a binary state per cell from a modular shift rule, producing an emergent diagonal texture never drawn as a diagonal directly. Motion is a continuous 2D scroll of the (exactly repeating) weave pattern through the viewport, deliberately NOT a whole-canvas rotation -- this sidesteps by construction the entire rotation/rectangular-viewport brightness-trend bug class voronoimosaic.html's write-up documents at length, since a scrolling periodic pattern has identical total coverage at every phase (the same trick stripweave.html already relies on).

Verified: validateEngine() 11/11 across seeds 1-10 plus the CLI's actual default seed 12345, margins comfortable throughout: projectedRise -1.1 to +1.3 (vs the 50 threshold, and unusually tight even by this pool's standards since a purely-scrolling periodic pattern has essentially zero coverage variance by construction), avgSat 71.1-93.8 (vs the 22 minimum), zero near-white pixels, fastMotion always comfortably above its per-frame floor. A genuinely new failure mode was found only by running validateEngine() across the full seed battery, not by reasoning about the code: the first design paired this per-tile bulge morph with a continuous whole-field rigid rotation (the field sized to the canvas half-diagonal, the widmanstatten.html/phasespikes.html technique, so a full rotation never reveals an empty corner) as a second, seemingly-free motion source. idea: Two literal, independently-rotating opaque dot lattices of the SAME spacing, one drawn over the other, clipped to a centred disk sized so the field's own inscribed circle always fully covers it regardless of rotation angle -- the large-scale beat pattern emerges purely from which dots visually occlude which as the two lattices' relative angle continuously sweeps, not from any computed interference field. reason: Guaranteed-minimum-magnitude, opposite-sign rotation rates for the two lattices (never derived as one rate plus a signed delta, which was considered and rejected before writing any code once it was clear the two terms could partially cancel toward a near-stalled second rate -- exactly the near-zero-motion bug class CLAUDE.md documents at length): rateA = sgn()*rand(0.4,0.7)*SPEED, rateB = -sign(rateA)*rand(0.4,0.7)*SPEED, guaranteeing both individual rates and their difference (the relative sweep speed the whole moire effect depends on) are always substantial. inspirationSource: Doyle spiral circle packing -- category "random Wikipedia article" (Wikipedia itself is blocked in this sandbox, so used the established fallback: an open WebSearch for an unusual/lesser-known geometric curve or tiling construction). A Doyle spiral is a packing of non-overlapping circles where every circle is tangent to exactly six neighbours (hexagonal combinatorics) yet the radii are NOT all equal -- they grow geometrically outward, so the circle centres fall on three families of interlocking logarithmic spiral arms. Discovered/formalised by Peter Doyle (independently used by van Iterson in 1907 to model phyllotaxis); it is the discrete analogue of the complex exponential map z -> exp(w) applied to a regular hexagonal circle packing. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doyle_spiral, https://www.josleys.com/articles/HexCirclePackings.pdf (Jos Leys, worked construction/rendering notes for the conformal-map approximation used), https://archive.bridgesmathart.org/2008/bridges2008-131.pdf (Sutcliffe, "Doyle Spiral Circle Packings Animated", prior art-rendering treatment).
idea: A hex lattice u(m,n) = m + n*exp(i*pi/3) mapped through w(u) = exp(C*u) for a complex growth constant C, with each circle's radius set to the local conformal-derivative scale |C*w|*0.5 -- an approximation verified offline to be extremely tight (worst-case tangency ratio 0.9962 across the used parameter range). A genuinely different construction principle from every other radial/spiral engine in the pool: not mirrored-wedge stamps (kaleidoscope.html), not a logarithmic spiral tile MARCH with edge-matched polygon segments (voderberg.html), not a golden-angle point-placement rule with no tangency constraint (phyllotaxis.html), not a Voronoi proximity partition (voronoimosaic.html) -- its defining invariant is circle-to-circle TANGENCY under fixed hexagonal combinatorics with every radius fixed by a conformal constraint, which nothing else in the pool uses as its generative primitive.
reason: Needed two real bug-driven redesigns, both found only by rendering and looking, not by reasoning about the formula. (1) The first draft sampled (m,n) over a SQUARE box, which maps via the hex lattice basis to a stretched rhombus in u-space -- its single farthest corner dominated the empirical max-reach scale calibration, so the rendered composition was a narrow, lopsided ARC of circles occupying a small corner of the frame, not a full disc. Root-caused via a standalone offline diagnostic script measuring angular-bin coverage at fixed radius levels; fixed by switching to a HEX-BALL sampling region (max(|m|,|n|,|m+n|) <= RANGE), verified algebraically to map to a near-regular hexagon (all 6 vertices at exactly the same Euclidean distance from the origin in u-space), plus narrowing growth/twist parameter ranges (growth in [0.05,0.10], |twist| in [0.15,0.19]) to guarantee a full angular sweep at every radius shell -- swept numerically until zero empty angular bins (of 16) was achieved across the whole tested range. (2) A first per-frame motion design (within-ring antiphase pulse, alternating adjacent circles) measured too weak for both validateEngine()'s fastMotion and compositionDrift gates (8/16 seeds failing) since local antiphase cancellation suppresses exactly the kind of real structural change compositionDrift needs to see. Replaced with a travelling radial breathing wave (WAVE_K=3 full spatial cycles), which initially assumed phasing by ring INDEX would sum to zero brightness change -- wrong, because the exponential map's outer rings hold vastly more total area than inner ones, so an index-uniform wave is not actually area-neutral (one seed projected +97.9 luma). Fixed by phasing the wave on cumulative AREA fraction instead of ring-count fraction (sort circles radially, accumulate r^2, use that cumulative fraction as the wave's spatial axis) -- an integer wave count across THIS axis sums to exactly zero at every instant regardless of how skewed the per-ring area distribution is. inspirationSource: Diffusion-limited aggregation (DLA) -- the Witten-Sander (1981) model behind electrodeposited metal "trees," frost/ice ferns on glass, mineral dendrites in rock veins, and Lichtenberg discharge channels, category "random natural structure" (deliberately picked as the pool's most under-used category recently, only hoppercrystal.html shipped from it since 2026-09-08). A seed particle sits fixed; new particles are released far away and random-walk until they either stick permanently at first contact with the existing cluster, or wander too far and are discarded and re-released. Because a random walker is statistically more likely to hit an exposed tip than penetrate a concave gap between branches, the growing structure self-reinforces at its tips, producing a sparse, highly branched fractal with a measured fractal dimension of D ~ 1.7 in 2D. Sources: https://users.math.yale.edu/public_html/People/frame/Fractals/Panorama/Physics/DLA/DLA.html (Witten-Sander model overview), https://arxiv.org/pdf/cond-mat/9402003 and https://johngavin.github.io/randomwalk/articles/dla_theory.html (D ~ 1.712 +/- 0.003 in 2D, measured via large-scale simulation), https://arxiv.org/pdf/1407.2586 (bias-free on-lattice DLA algorithm, the release/kill-radius convention followed here).
idea: 3-4 independent DLA clusters grown once per video via on-lattice random-walk accretion (big-step accelerated, radius-targeted termination for render-init speed), each cell's arrival order recorded so a periodic reveal-sweep can play back the growth history as a time-lapse without ever re-simulating a walk at render time. A genuinely different construction principle from dendrite.html, the pool's only other branching engine: dendrite.html is a deterministic recursive rule (every segment spawns exactly two shorter, angularly-offset children, fully fixed the instant its parameters are drawn); DLA has no branching rule at all -- the shape is the literal sequential history of thousands of independent random walks and one local stickiness test, with branchiness and tip-splitting as emergent statistical consequences, not an authored rule. Also distinct from automaton.html (synchronous full-row CA update every generation vs. DLA's particle-based sequential accretion).

Replaced with a coverage-neutral size/brightness wave phased by arrival-order INDEX FRACTION (an integer wave count across that axis, the same 'phase spans whole cycles' invariant orbweb.html/doylespiral.html established) applied across ALL revealed cells rather than just the growth tip -- safe here (unlike liesegang.html's ring case) because every DLA cell is the same size/shape, so index-fraction phasing is exactly linear in brightness, not subject to the additive-overlap-saturation trap liesegang.html's write-up documents. idea: An IMBRICATED (overlapping, shingled) lattice of elongated ellipse "scale" shapes in staggered brick-offset rows, with each row drawn OVER the row below it (real roof-tile/fish-scale overlap, not a non-overlapping tiling). A genuinely different construction principle from every textile/lattice engine already in the pool: not opaque non-overlapping vertical strips (stripweave.html), not a single grid with one binary over/under state from a modular shift rule (herringbone.html), not continuous per-thread positional misalignment noise around one fixed motif (ikatweave.html), not static discrete shapes charted on a grid plus a choreography layer (taniko.html), not a per-unit rotation state driving foreshortening (tabletweave.html). Colour is not a plain hue rotation but a direct rendering of 'orientation-dependent reflection': each scale is assigned a fixed RANK FRACTION (0..1, evenly spaced by count) along a fixed spatial sweep axis, and hue = base + spread*cos(2*pi*waveK*rankFraction - sweepPhase) for an integer waveK and one shared, continuously advancing sweepPhase -- a coherent iridescent colour band sweeps across the whole surface exactly like a real wing's colour shifting with viewing angle. An independent second rank ordering (perpendicular spatial axis) drives a decorrelated per-scale SIZE-breathing wave for unit-level motion.
reason: Coverage-neutrality for both the hue sweep and the size-breathing wave rests on the same rank-fraction technique this pool's rosenspikes.html/doylespiral.html/frostgrowth.html already established: N elements assigned rankFrac = i/N (evenly spaced by count) and a wave phased at 2*pi*waveK*rankFrac for an integer waveK sums to exactly zero at every instant, independent of the shared phase offset, by discrete-Fourier orthogonality. Verified OFFLINE before writing any rendering code (the same discipline this pool's quasicrystal.html/geodome.html/hilbertweave.html/spaceframe.html already established for a claim that could look plausible even if subtly wrong): a standalone script confirmed sum_i cos(2*pi*k*(i/N) - phase) is exactly zero (floating-point-exact, ~1e-14) across every tested N/k/phase combination. This gave high confidence the design would be validate.js-safe from the first draft, and it was: validateEngine() passed 16/16 on the FIRST attempt across seeds 1-15 plus the CLI's actual default seed 12345 -- no iteration needed, joining primespiral.html/stripweave.html/widmanstatten.html/hoppercrystal.html/moire.html/orbweb.html as engines that passed cleanly on the first attempt by applying this pool's established coverage-stability and motion lessons from the start. Deliberately NO whole-field rotation at all (per truchet.html's lesson that a reflexive whole-field rotation only dilutes the mandatory unit-motion signal by dominating the rigid-fit unless fastMotion genuinely needs it as a second source) -- the hue sweep and size breathing alone gave unitMotionNonRigidFrac exactly 1.0 on every single tested seed, since neither a colour change nor an independent per-scale size oscillation at a fixed screen position can be explained by any single rigid transform. Margins comfortable throughout: avgSat 66.2-91.8 (vs the 22 minimum), zero near-white pixels on every seed, projectedRise -20.3 to +24.4 (vs the 50 threshold), compositionDrift 0.0347-0.0767 (vs the 0.015 minimum), fastMotion always far above its per-frame floor (17-45 vs floors of 2.3-4.9), projectedHourRenderMin 38.7-52.5min (well inside the CI budget). Visual spot-checks across 2/25/50/75/95/105% of a 40s cycle at 3 seeds, actually rendering PNGs and looking at them, not just reading validator output: a vivid, bold, immediately-recognisable imbricated scale/shell texture with a genuine diagonal iridescent colour band visibly sweeping across the frame between checkpoints, clear crisp scale outlines and ridge-highlight texture, and three visually distinct palette combinations (green/orange/yellow; blue/purple/cyan Morpho-style; aqua/green/orange) across the three spot-checked seeds.

inspirationSource: Tensegrity / "floating compression" -- Kenneth Snelson's structural principle (discovered 1948, before Buckminster Fuller coined the "tensegrity" portmanteau), category "random architectural or typographic movement" (picked to vary away from "obscure mathematical object" and "a random featured image", used the two prior days, per the herringbone.html precedent of varying categories rather than defaulting to a heavily-used one). Rigid compression members (struts) never touch one another at all -- each is individually suspended, held apart and together purely by a network of continuously taut tension members (cables), a condition Snelson called "continuous tension, discontinuous compression". His sculptures (most famously "Needle Tower") are built from a stack of identical twisted 3-strut prism modules, each rotated relative to the one below. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tensegrity, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Snelson (search snippets only -- Wikipedia is blocked in this sandbox), http://kennethsnelson.net/Tensegrity_and_Weaving.pdf.
idea: A chain of twisted triangular tensegrity-prism modules stacked along one axis, rendered horizontally (not vertically like Needle Tower itself) so the twisting structure fills a 16:9 frame rather than occupying a thin vertical strip. Each pair of adjacent rings (3 shared vertices) is connected by 3 diagonal struts (skew connections between a bottom vertex and a DIFFERENT top vertex, verified offline to never come near touching each other); each ring's own 3 edges are the tension cables. A genuinely different construction principle from every other real-WebGL engine in the pool: not sparse orbiting solids, not a grid of spinning cubes, not lit tori, not one continuous convex mesh, not a CONNECTED strut framework where every beam meets at shared rigid joints (spaceframe.html's octet truss -- a dense, solid-feeling lattice), not a concave excavation, not a lattice of concave niche cells or convex spikes -- the pool's first "discontinuous compression" structure: rigid bars that never touch each other at all, giving an open, airy silhouette that is the structural OPPOSITE of spaceframe.html's dense truss.
reason: The core geometry (strut non-touching, strut length safety under the planned per-ring wobble) was verified OFFLINE before writing any rendering code, the same discipline this pool's quasicrystal.html/geodome.html/hilbertweave.html/spaceframe.html already established: a standalone script confirmed that for TWIST angles in 100-135 degrees, the 3 struts within one tensegrity-prism tier never come within less than 0.32-0.55 (ring-spacing units) of touching each other (comfortably clear of the ~0.1-unit strut width used), and that under a +-35 degree per-ring angular wobble, strut length stays in a safe, non-degenerate band (1.18-1.59 vs a 1.47 baseline, no near-zero collapse). A real visual-quality defect was found only by rendering and looking, not caught by any numeric gate: the first design (5-10 tiers at radius 0.55-0.72) rendered as a thin horizontal strip across the vertical centre of the frame, most of the canvas left as unused black margin -- directly against the house style's 'fills the frame boldly' preference, because the chain's length:diameter ratio (~11.7:1) was far more elongated than the 16:9 frame. Fixed by treating tier count and radius as a function of the CANVAS aspect ratio rather than free parameters: 4-7 tiers at radius 1.15-1.5 gives a length:diameter ratio close to 16:9 (5 tiers * 1.0 spacing = 5 long, 2*1.4 radius = 2.8 across, ratio 1.79). Unit-level dynamics were built in from the first draft (per CLAUDE.md's 2026-09-10 standing requirement) and deliberately include NO whole-structure rotation at all (per truchet.html's lesson that a reflexive whole-field rotation only dilutes the mandatory unit-motion signal by dominating the rigid-fit unless fastMotion genuinely needs it): each ring has its own independent angular wobble (guaranteed-minimum-magnitude, random sign, rate/phase), which leaves cables exactly length-invariant (rotating a rigid triangle about the chain axis never changes its own side lengths) while making every strut (spanning between two independently-wobbling rings) visibly flex relative to its neighbours -- no single rigid transform can explain many independently-wobbling rings at once. validateEngine() across seeds 1-15 plus the CLI's actual default seed 12345 initially passed 15/16, with seed 13 failing fastMotion on a thin margin (5.64 vs a 6.31 floor -- an unlucky coincidence of several independently-random wobble phases landing near their own zero-angular-velocity point simultaneously at the 1.5s sample window, the same class of risk torusrings3d.html's write-up documents for its own wobble). Fixed by raising wobble amplitude (12-20 to 16-24 degrees) and rate (0.5-0.85 to 0.65-1.05 rad/s, still comfortably inside the offline-verified safe band up to 35 degrees) for more margin; re-validated 16/16, seed 13's fastMotion improved to 13.97 vs its 6.35 floor. Final validateEngine() 16/16 across seeds 1-15 plus 12345: avgSat 50.4-63.1 (vs the 22 minimum), zero near-white pixels on every seed, projectedRise -14.7 to +23.6 (vs the 50 threshold), compositionDrift 0.0278-0.0567 (vs the 0.015 minimum), unitMotionNonRigidFrac 0.978-1.0 (vs the 0.40 minimum -- no thin-margin seeds after the fix), fastMotion always comfortably above its per-frame floor, projectedHourRenderMin 32.2-92.2min (well inside the CI budget). Visual spot-checks across 2/25/50/75/95/105% of a 43.5s cycle at 3 seeds, actually rendering PNGs and looking at them, not just reading validator output: a vivid, bold, immediately-recognisable open zigzag lattice of twisted floating struts with clearly visible taut cable triangles, filling the 16:9 frame boldly after the aspect-ratio fix, no clipping or artifacts at any tested fraction, and three visually distinct palette combinations (green-to-blue rainbow, orange-to-teal, red-to-green) across seeds.

inspirationSource: Columnar basalt jointing (Giant's Causeway) -- category "random natural structure". Real fracture-mechanics physics: as lava cools from the top down, thermal-contraction cracks initially form 90-degree T-junctions, then mechanically relax toward 120-degree Y-junctions (the angle that best dissipates stress), producing a near-hexagonal (statistically 4-9 sided) polygon tiling with essentially no gaps -- the same physical principle behind mudcrack networks and drying-paint craquelure, just at basalt scale. Sources: physicsworld.com, smithsonianmag.com, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giant%27s_Causeway.
idea: A field of solid polygonal PRISMS (columns) of varying height, packed EDGE-TO-EDGE with no gaps at all, viewed at an oblique elevated angle looking down across the column tops -- the pool's only engine that takes an existing, already offline-verified 2D partition construction (voronoimosaic.html's proven half-plane-intersection Voronoi cell algorithm, reused verbatim) and EXTRUDES it into a real lit 3D scene. A genuinely different composition from every other real-WebGL engine in the pool: not sparse orbiting solids, not a grid of spinning cubes, not lit tori, not one continuous convex dome mesh, not a connected strut framework, not a concave excavation or niche-cell lattice, not independently-growing spikes, not a floating tensegrity chain -- a dense field of individually-heighted, gap-free polygonal columns.
reason: The Voronoi cell footprint construction (clipHalfPlane/intersectEdge/voronoiCell) was reused verbatim from the already offline-verified voronoimosaic.html rather than re-derived. The top-cap triangle fan's vertex winding was verified by HAND ALGEBRA (not rendering, since the render/validate toolchain was transiently unavailable when this was first drafted): an explicit cross-product computation on sample coordinates caught and fixed a real downward-facing-normal bug before any frame was ever rendered, later confirmed correct once rendering resumed. Colour is tied to each column's fixed footprint centroid angle (rotation-axis-invariant); height follows a rank-fraction-phased travelling wave (the doylespiral.html/rosenspikes.html/frostgrowth.html technique, exactly zero-sum by discrete-Fourier orthogonality regardless of the Voronoi cells' non-uniform spatial distribution), deliberately with NO whole-scene rotation (per truchet.html's lesson). A persistent validate.js speed-budget failure survived several real fixes (a redundant per-frame GPU re-upload of the static colour buffer; per-frame array allocation in the position-writing hot path, replaced with precomputed per-cell Y-index lists so only the changed height coordinate is touched each frame; a redundant per-frame recomputation/reallocation of the fully-static camera view/MVP matrices) before the real remaining cause was found: this engine is a full-bleed, edge-to-edge column field (the house-style "fills the frame" requirement applied literally, with far less black background than sparser WebGL engines like rosenspikes.html), so multisample antialiasing was multiplying fragment-shading cost across nearly the whole frame under software (swiftshader) rendering. Disabling antialiasing (antialias: false) was the fix that actually resolved it: avgMsPerFrame dropped from a consistently-failing 76-133ms (often exceeding the 100ms budget, with worst-frame spikes up to 2688ms blowing the 2000ms single-frame cap) to a comfortably-passing 39-88ms across the full seed battery. The full 16-seed battery then surfaced a second, genuinely different failure: seed 1 failed compositionDrift at 0.0114 (need >= 0.015) -- the height-breathing wave's amplitude (+-22%) was too subtle from this camera's oblique angle to register enough rotation-invariant structural change over the 300s test window, even though it is real, non-rigid, per-column motion. Fixed by raising the wave amplitude to +-30%, re-verified across all 16 seeds with no regression to any other check.

inspirationSource: Gosper curve (flowsnake) -- Category: random Wikipedia article (Wikipedia is blocked in this sandbox, so an open WebSearch for an unusual/lesser-known geometric curve construction was used instead, the established fallback for this category). A fractal space-filling curve built on a HEXAGONAL lattice rather than a square one, via its standard L-system (axiom A, rules A -> A-B--B+A++AA+B-, B -> +A-BB--B-A++A+B, 60-degree turns) -- a REP-7 substitution, where 7 small self-similar copies of the bounded "Gosper island" tile one larger copy of itself. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gosper_curve (search snippets only).
idea: The curve was expanded to order 3 (343 segments) and tagged per-segment by which of the 7 top-level rep-7 branches it descends from (verified offline to reconstruct the byte-identical curve while carrying the tag), with hue tied to that tag -- a direct visualisation of the curve's own 7-fold recursive structure, deliberately not a linear fold-order gradient (dragonfold.html's technique) to stay distinct at the composition level, not just the construction level.
reason: Built engines/manual/gosper.html but could not find a design that reliably clears BOTH the mandatory novelty gate (nearest-neighbour fingerprint distance >= 0.60) and validate.js's fastMotion check together, despite many substantively different iterations (well past the routine's ~4-round budget), because every lever that helped one gate directly hurt the other. (1) The first design (discrete filled rounded-square blocks along the curve, one dense centred instance) measured 0.487 vs auto-2026-08-30-scenic-view-of-gardens -- a per-feature z-score diagnostic showed coverage/blobCount/edgeDensity nearly identical to that neighbour. (2) Enlarging the instance and thickening blocks to raise coverage (the diagnostic's clearest lever) made it WORSE, not better: 0.430 vs starburst, because the whole composition was deeper inside this pool's broad 'compact centred mass' archetype cluster (starburst/torusrings3d/solids3d/auto-spirograph/scenic-view-of-gardens/poets-henj/lattice3d/geodome/voderberg -- a 10-member perceptual-archetype group at threshold 0.55), not just close to one specific neighbour. (3) Switching from discrete blocks to a continuous connected stroke (same hue-by-branch scheme, vertices on the path stroked with glow) moved the right direction (0.554) by breaking an exact blobCount/blobSizeCV/largestBlobFrac match with starburst (both engines measured as a single solid blob to 2 decimal places), but still fell short. (4) Splitting the curve's 7 rep-7 branches into visibly separate islands (each branch's points pulled toward its own centroid, the bridging segment between branches never drawn) plus a small irregular per-branch radial/tangential scatter (to break the near-even 7-fold ring's own rotational symmetry, which was itself colliding with torusrings3d/lattice3d) reached 0.626 vs torusrings3d at a tuned side/scatter combination -- confirmed as a genuine local peak: both a larger scatter+smaller instance (0.538, collided with hilbertweave's multi-instance archetype instead) and a larger instance+more scatter (0.593) moved the WRONG direction when tested. (5) At that passing composition, the per-vertex bob wobble amplitude needed to stay small (pitch*0.10-0.20) to avoid visually tearing the connected stroke apart, which left validate.js's fastMotion check failing on 14/16 seeds (motion too slow to read as exciting). Boosting wobble RATE alone (per the ikatweave.html precedent that unit-motion/fastMotion gates are rate-sensitive while the novelty gate's static-frame fingerprint is amplitude-sensitive) barely moved fastMotion margins (the sampled 1.5s window already spans most of a half-cycle even at the original rate, so further rate increases mostly just complete MORE cycles rather than reaching further per sample) and still cost novelty margin (0.604, thin). Boosting wobble AMPLITUDE instead fixed fastMotion decisively (16/16 passed, comfortable margins) but collapsed novelty to 0.534 -- back below threshold. A moderate amplitude between the two extremes (0.580) and a strengthened travelling brightness/width pulse as an orthogonal lever (0.538) each independently failed novelty too. Every tested motion lever that gave fastMotion enough margin to pass reliably also moved the static-frame composition measurably closer to this pool's existing 'scattered bright blob cluster' and multi-instance-curve-chain archetypes (hilbertweave/dragonfold) already occupying this novelty neighbourhood -- strong, repeated, measured evidence of a structural conflict between this composition family and the fastMotion gate's magnitude requirement, not a tuning problem. Per the routine's explicit guidance, shipping nothing is strictly better than shipping a near-duplicate or an engine that unreliably fails a mandatory quality gate. A genuinely different motion mechanism decoupled from both spatial amplitude and pulse width/brightness (e.g. per-branch independent ROTATION about each island's own centre, which doesn't require moving individual vertices far from their rest position but can still register as fast per-pixel change at the island's own edges) would be needed to revisit this idea.

inspirationSource: Nematic liquid crystal "schlieren texture" -- category "obscure mathematical object / crystal system / physical phenomenon" (tied as the pool's most under-used category recently alongside "a random featured image"; picked since it was last used 2026-09-26 vs. 2026-09-27 for the other). An open WebSearch for an unusual physical pattern-formation phenomenon surfaced the real optical pattern seen when a nematic liquid crystal sample is viewed between crossed polarizers: dark "brushes" radiating from point DISCLINATIONS (defects in the molecular orientation field), 4|s| brushes per defect of topological strength s (s = +-1/2, +-1 are the physically observed strengths). Sources (search snippets): https://www.personal.kent.edu/~bisenyuk/liquidcrystals/textures1.html, https://doitpoms.ac.uk/tlplib/liquid_crystals/observing_defects.php.
idea: The nematic director's orientation angle theta(x,y) at any point is the sum of each point-defect's own harmonic contribution, theta(x,y) = SUM_i s_i * atan2(y-y_i, x-x_i) -- the same mathematics as superposing point vortices in 2D potential flow (atan2 is the harmonic conjugate of log|z-z_i|), chosen because theta must be harmonic (minimising Frank elastic energy in the one-constant approximation gives Laplace's equation) with the correct winding number (2*pi*s_i) around each defect. Crossed-polarizer intensity I = sin^2(2*theta - 2*P) (P = polarizer angle) was re-mapped via a smoothstep + percentile rank-select into thin dark brush lines separating flat, vivid colour wedges (a crisp pinwheel), rather than the raw formula's soft gradient, to satisfy the house style's "crisp, not organic blobs" rule. A genuinely different construction principle from every other engine in the pool: not a wave-interference field sampled for its zero-crossing (chladni) or ranked maxima (phasespikes) or two rotating lattices (moire) -- a harmonic SINGULARITY/VORTEX superposition.
reason: Built engines/manual/schlieren.html. VERIFIED OFFLINE before writing any rendering code: winding number around an isolated defect matched 2*pi*s_i (within 1e-3) for integer strengths, brush count exactly matched the physically documented 4*|s| for all tested strengths (1, -1, 0.5, -0.5), the rendered intensity I=sin^2(2*theta-2*P) was perfectly continuous (floating-point noise only, 1e-5 to 1e-7) across an individual defect's own atan2 branch-cut ray, and a shared polarizer angle P(t) rotates each defect's brush pattern at angular rate exactly 1/s_i (measured: dAngle/dP = 1.000 for s=1, 2.000 for s=0.5, matching the analytic dark-brush-condition derivation exactly) -- the engine's primary motion mechanism, giving genuinely differentiated per-defect motion from one shared time-varying parameter with no per-element choreography needed. First render read as soft organic blobs (smooth sin^2 gradient between brushes), directly against the house style -- fixed by sharpening the brush mapping via a smoothstep and posterising the hue into discrete wedges, turning the same phase field into a crisp pinwheel. That design then failed validateEngine() 4/16 (2 real brightness-trend whiteout failures up to +86 luma projected, 2 unit-motion failures where a lucky-same-strength defect draw let one rigid rotation explain most of the frame's motion). Root-caused and fixed in three rounds: (1) applied chladni.html's rank-select percentile technique to hold the dark-brush band's AREA exactly constant every frame (a fixed |sin(phase)| threshold let dark-band area swing as the polarizer angle P swept through this multi-defect field's non-uniform phase density) -- this alone fixed most seeds but one got WORSE (+64 to +226 luma), revealing a SECOND, independent instance of the same bug: different HUE_BANDS have different inherent luma at fixed lightness/saturation (the well-documented hue-affects-luma trap), and a plain linear phaseWrap->band mapping let each band's area swing too -- fixed by rank-selecting hue bands into exactly equal-area groups as well, which eliminated the whiteout failures entirely (16/16 passed that check after this fix); (2) guaranteed defect strength diversity (forcing at least one magnitude-1 and one magnitude-2 defect, since brush angular rate is 1/s) to prevent an all-same-rate draw from reading as one rigid rotation -- fixed most but not all unit-motion failures, since a MAJORITY (not just one) of defects landing on the same magnitude group could still dominate; (3) switched to a balanced-shuffle magnitude assignment (near-even split of defects between the two rate groups, not just one forced of each) plus a substantially strengthened independent defect-position orbit drift as a magnitude-independent motion source, which resolved the remaining failures: validateEngine() 16/16 across seeds 1-15 + 12345, avgSat 69.8-97.1 (vs the 22 minimum), zero near-white pixels, projectedRise -18.9 to +17.8 (vs the 50 threshold), compositionDrift 0.033-0.106 (vs the 0.015 minimum), unitMotionNonRigidFrac 0.445-0.96 (vs the 0.40 minimum), projectedHourRenderMin 43.5-50.5min (comfortably inside the CI budget). Novelty gate: first measured at 0.631 vs auto-2026-08-27-field-of-small-lit-3d-solids-drifting-th -- a per-feature z-score diagnostic showed the collision driven by periodicity/mirror/orientation features, which CLAUDE.md documents as NOT rotation-invariant; tried adding a slow whole-field rotation to shift those features, but this measured WORSE (0.610, against a different neighbour) -- reverted, confirming once more that not every lever moves novelty distance in the expected direction. Shipped at the original, reverted design's measured distance (0.631), a clean pass above the 0.60 minimum. Visual spot-checks across 2/25/50/75/95/105% of a 36s cycle at multiple seeds, actually rendering PNGs and looking at them: vivid, bold, immediately-recognisable crisp colour pinwheels with dark radiating brush lines, smooth continuous evolution across the cycle-boundary reconfigure with no jarring jump, and genuinely distinct defect-count/palette combinations across seeds.
